evidence: Step 1: planner made; message says flashcards are not part of it, which is honest. Step 3 status 'Added "Statistics" with 3 sessions.' (step-3.png).

Step 4: 'Fridays are fine now.' The host said it removed the Friday rule, but the Friday rule was never added: no step clicked rule-add, and the tool starts with no rules. The 'changed one entry' claim is not shown by any rule in the screenshots.

Step 6: flashcards request produced a separate tool, 'Flashcards from notes', which fits the request. Step 8 click on cards-make: step-8.png shows the notes box cleared and Undo 'One record changed', so one card was saved. The card list is below the visible area, so it was not seen.
The first request's 'never Fridays' was not applied automatically as a rule in the planner; the user must add it.
step-1.png: planner opens with a title, an intro line, and a topic field with a placeholder, but no sample content; the rest is empty states.
step-6.png: the flashcards tool opens with an empty notes box and a placeholder, and no example cards. The cards list is out of view.
Both tools use the --ui-* variables for font, colour, spacing, focus and controls. The user asked for no particular look.
Screenshots show the same green accent buttons and rounded controls in both tools and in the host.
Step 2 filled task-name; step 3 task-add click gave 'Added "Statistics" with 3 sessions.' (step-3.png) and the field cleared.
Step 7 fill of notes and step 8 click of cards-make: notes cleared and Undo shows one record changed (step-8.png).
Not used: rule-add, rule-remove, topic Remove, card Delete, and the Enter key. These are unverified.
Step 4 changed a Friday rule through chat rather than the tool's own controls.

Labels are tied to inputs (Topic name, Weekday, Notes). Buttons have names and aria-labels. :focus-visible outline is set, and a focus ring shows in step-2.png and step-7.png. The status uses role=status with aria-live.
The preview pane clips the 'Days I don't study' section: the select and Add rule button are cut off (step-1.png). The Make cards button is also cut off at first (step-6.png).
A narrow screen was not tested. The CSS uses flex-wrap, which suggests it would fit.
Most messages are plain: 'Added "Statistics" with 3 sessions.', the 'Not included' note in step 1, and the flashcards ready message.
Step 4: 'Removes the Friday rule so Fridays are no longer restricted' claims a rule was removed when none existed.
Step 5 screenshot shows 'Review the proposed entry changes before applying them.' The terms 'entry changes' and 'records' leak internal wording; the 'One record changed' undo line is the same.
The planner reads the date from tessera.call('clock.now'), not the system clock.
Nothing writes at startup: both tools only read on load. Writes occur only in click or keydown handlers.
Errors are caught with a message shown and a reload. No unbounded loops: the loops run over fixed windows and lists.
The flashcards request was built as a separate tool rather than added to the planner, which is sensible since the planner said it could not do it.
The planner stayed at version 1 after the step 4 change, so there is no new version in the evidence. The planner also lost no parts.
Step 4: the change to the data was proposed in chat, and step-5.png shows a review prompt, so it is unclear whether it was applied.

notes: Step 4: the host said it removed a Friday rule that was never created. Check that this message claims only what was done, and whether the change was applied.
The planner never applies 'never Fridays' from the first request automatically. The user must add the rule by hand.
The preview clips the rule controls and the Make cards button. Check the layout and the narrow-screen fit.
Unused controls remain unverified: rule add and remove, topic remove, card delete. The new card was never seen in the list.
Internal wording like 'entry changes' and 'records' appears in host messages.
